Density of the Product of Two Normal Random Variables

Source: R/dprodnormal.R
dprodnormal.Rd

Evaluates the exact probability density function of \(XY\), where \((X, Y)\) is bivariate normal. It is the density companion to pprodnormal and qprodnormal and uses no Monte Carlo simulation.

Usage

dprodnormal(x, mu.x, mu.y, se.x = 1, se.y = 1, rho = 0, log = FALSE)

Arguments

x

numeric vector of values at which to evaluate the density (the value of the product).

mu.x, mu.y

means of \(X\) and \(Y\).

se.x, se.y

standard deviations of \(X\) and \(Y\); must be positive.

rho

correlation between \(X\) and \(Y\); must satisfy \(-1 < \rho < 1\). The default is 0.

log

logical; if TRUE, the logarithm of the density is returned.

Value

A numeric vector of densities (or log densities), one per element of x.

Details

For general means and correlation the density is the one-dimensional integral \(f(z) = \int f_{X,Y}(x, z/x)\,|x|^{-1}\,dx\) (Rohatgi; Glen et al., 2004), evaluated by adaptive quadrature over the range that carries the mass of the conditioning variable and split at the sign change at zero. When both means are zero the closed form $$f(z) = \frac{\exp\{\rho z/(1-\rho^2)\}\, K_0\{|z|/(1-\rho^2)\}}{\pi\sqrt{1-\rho^2}}$$ (unit variances; rescaled here) is used instead, with \(K_0\) the modified Bessel function of the second kind (Nadarajah and Pogany, 2016; Gaunt, 2019). The two agree to near machine precision.

The density is infinite at exactly x = 0 for every parameter setting (a logarithmic singularity: \(XY\) is near zero whenever either factor is), so dprodnormal(0, ...) returns Inf. Plot it on a grid that avoids 0 and clip the vertical axis.

References

Craig, C. C. (1936). On the frequency function of xy. Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 7, 1–15.

Glen, A. G., Leemis, L. M. and Drew, J. H. (2004). Computing the distribution of the product of two continuous random variables. Computational Statistics & Data Analysis, 44, 451–464.

Nadarajah, S. and Pogany, T. K. (2016). On the distribution of the product of correlated normal random variables. Comptes Rendus Mathematique, 354, 201–204.

See also

pprodnormal, qprodnormal

Examples

dprodnormal(c(-0.1, 0.05, 0.3), mu.x = 0.5, mu.y = 0.3, se.x = 0.2, se.y = 0.4, rho = 0.3)
#> [1] 0.8608815 2.1079806 1.1210739

# the density integrates to the CDF
integrate(dprodnormal, 0.001, 0.3, mu.x = 0.5, mu.y = 0.3, se.x = 0.2, se.y = 0.4)$value
#> [1] 0.5488999
pprodnormal(0.3, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.4) - pprodnormal(0.001, 0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0.4)
#> [1] 0.5488999
